title: BGN with TWO independent priced chains (K 1 -> 2 priced states beyond the rate) and three types whose loading vectors span them, at bvych0's loading sizes and total price
question: Group 4 (larger factor models): does a second priced state, with types loading on both, raise the room and the fair gap in BGN as the latent-product reduced form predicts, or lower the gap as KP's vym3 did?
notes: Campaign 2026-10-12, group 4 cell for BGN (docs/CAMPAIGN_REPORT_2026-10-11). The control is bvych0 (one 21-node chain, type_bv (0.01, 0.035, 0.07), gamma_v 2.5). Here y2 is a second 21-node Tauchen chain, independent of y1, with the same kappa; the state is the joint node (441 nodes), the J* programme and every table run on it, and the panel exports y2_stand beside y_stand so the fair linear benchmark sees both states. Loading VECTORS: type 0 0.01 (1, 0), type 1 0.035 (0, 1), type 2 0.07 (1, 1)/sqrt(2): the same sizes as bvych0 in three directions, so the cross-section of exposures is two-dimensional. Total price of y-risk unchanged, ||gamma|| = 2.5 split as 2.5/sqrt(2) per chain (vym3's convention). Validation: with a dead second chain (type_bv2 0, gamma_v2 0) the joint-chain code reproduces the single chain's bases to 2e-13; at these parameters the Euler check on the joint chain is 2.3e-14 and type_theta (1, 1.0744, 1.287).
